title: Horses kept at Botai
description: People of the Botai settlement milk and probably ride horses, among the earliest evidence of horse husbandry.

title: Golden Man burial
description: A Saka noble is buried in a suit covered with some 4,000 gold ornaments, now a national symbol of Kazakhstan.

title: Samanids take Taraz
description: Ismail Samani captures the Karluk city of Taraz and turns its main church into a mosque, spreading Islam on the steppe frontier.

title: Death of Ahmad Yasawi
description: The Sufi poet who spread Islam among the Turkic nomads dies at Yasi, and his tomb becomes a place of pilgrimage.

title: Siege of Otrar
description: The Mongols take the town whose governor had killed their merchants, the opening of Genghis Khan's conquest of Central Asia.

title: Mausoleum of Ahmad Yasawi begun
description: Timur orders a great domed shrine over the Sufi's grave, which remains unfinished at his death.

title: Kazakh Khanate founded
description: Janibek and Kerei lead their followers out of the Uzbek Khanate and found a state of their own in Zhetysu.

title: Dzungar invasion
description: Dzungar armies overrun the southern steppe and drive the Kazakhs into a flight remembered as the Barefooted Flight.

title: Junior Jüz accepts Russian protection
description: Abul Khair Khan swears allegiance to the Russian empress Anna, the first step in Russia's absorption of the Kazakh steppe.

title: Kenesary's rebellion
place: Kazakh steppe (shown at Akmola, now Astana)
description: Kenesary Kasymov, the last Kazakh khan, fights Russian rule for ten years until he is killed in Kyrgyz territory.

title: Fort Verny founded
description: Russia builds a fort at the foot of the Tian Shan, which grows into the city of Almaty.

title: Revolt of 1916
description: Kazakhs and other Central Asians rise against conscription for wartime labour, and the revolt is put down with heavy loss of life.

title: Alash Autonomy proclaimed
description: A congress of Kazakh leaders declares a self-governing Kazakh state, which lasts until the Bolsheviks dissolve it in 1920.

title: Kazakh autonomous republic created
description: The Soviet government forms the Kirghiz Autonomous Socialist Soviet Republic, the first Soviet Kazakh state.

title: Karlag camp set up
description: One of the largest camps of the Gulag is established to supply labour for the mines and farms of central Kazakhstan.

title: Kazakh SSR created
description: Kazakhstan is raised to a full union republic of the Soviet Union.

title: Virgin Lands campaign begins
description: Khrushchev's drive to plough the northern steppe for grain brings hundreds of thousands of settlers to Kazakhstan.

title: Jeltoqsan protests
description: Students protest when Moscow replaces the Kazakh party leader Dinmukhamed Kunaev with a Russian from outside the republic, and troops break up the demonstrations by force.

title: Semipalatinsk test site closed
description: Nursultan Nazarbayev closes the site where the Soviet Union had carried out 456 nuclear tests over forty years.

title: Independence
description: Kazakhstan declares independence, the last Soviet republic to do so.

title: Alma-Ata Protocol
description: Leaders of eleven Soviet republics agree that the Soviet Union has ceased to exist and join the Commonwealth of Independent States.

title: Capital moved to Astana
description: The seat of government moves from Almaty to Akmola in the northern steppe, renamed Astana the next year.

title: Kokaral Dam completed
description: A dyke separates the northern Aral Sea from the rest, and its water level and fishery begin to recover after decades of shrinking.

title: Zhanaozen shootings
description: Police fire on striking oil workers on Independence Day and kill at least 14 people.

title: Nazarbayev resigns
description: Nursultan Nazarbayev steps down after nearly thirty years as president, and the capital is renamed Nur-Sultan in his honour.
